newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil - Prices seen softer on rising harvests.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil - Prices seen softer on rising harvests.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to slide further this week due to prospects of better harvests from both the Philippines and Indonesia, Manila vegetable oil traders said on Monday.
"Expect prices to weaken further. Tonnes of copra from all parts of the Philippines are pushing prices down," a senior Manila trader said.
He expected Philippine coconut oil shipments to U.S. and Europe to rise to 80,000 tonnes this month compared with 70,000 last month.
Philippine traders said Manila exported between 60,000 and 65,000 tonnes of coconut oil per month in the first quarter of the year.
They also said coconut oil exports from Indonesia had been rising in the past four months.

Trade group United Coconut Association of the Philippines said buyers of coconut oil quoted an average of $647.50 per tonne FOB last week compared to the previous $660. Sellers also quoted a lower price at $659.25 per tonne FOB from $669.50.
Coconut oil stocks in Rotterdam, however, dropped to 21,426 tonnes as of April 28 from the previous week's 22,305.
In the domestic market, coconut oil also dropped to 17.30 pesos per kg from 17.80 on April 29. Copra also softened to 10.50 pesos per kg from 11.30.
